title: Formal Substrate Change Record
description: The release classification one change carries (CAS-ADR-008). Every change that touches the published contract adds one record as a YAML file under docs/fs/changes/unreleased/. A record carries no version number: the release step assigns every unreleased record to the release that publishes it, folding the records into the manifest's revision_history and deleting the files, so concurrent changes add independent files rather than contending for the next number. The file name is a short kebab-case slug describing the change; it is not read.

classification.description: Whether the change is released as a patch, which needs no versioning act, or requires a new minor release because it crosses one of the three minor boundaries. A contract comparison finding a minor-level change refuses a patch classification unless detector_override records why.

category.description: The minor boundaries the change crosses; required for a minor and absent for a patch. More than one applies where several do.

items.description: capability: a caller can do something it could not do before. caller-adaptation: a caller must change what it does, or its current calls change meaning. operator-adaptation: someone running CAS must act beyond deploying the new build.

summary.description: What changed and why, for maintainers: the substrate artifacts touched and the shape of the change. Becomes the change's entry in the release's revision history.

for_callers.description: Release-note text a caller or operator needs, in one or two sentences. Required and non-empty for a minor; empty or omitted for a pure patch.

detector_override.description: The project owner's explicit downgrade of the contract comparison's findings for this change, recorded in the change for review. It covers the change's findings as a whole. Present only when the comparison finds a minor-level change that the owner has judged a patch, such as declaring behaviour the server already had; the gate warns when no finding remains to override.

reason.description: Why the finding asks nothing new of callers, stated so a reviewer can check it.

deprecates.description: What this change deprecates (CAS-ADR-008 clause 8). Each element is marked on the published contract in the same change -- deprecated: true in a specification, a description opening with Deprecated: in the MCP catalog -- except a deprecated value, value format or default, which only its parameter's description can state. The release that publishes this record dates the deprecation.

surface.description: The published artifact the pointer addresses: the SAGE Core API specification, the CAS Application API specification, or the MCP tool catalog.

pointer.description: The element, in the contract comparison's pointer form: paths/{path}/{method}, then /parameters/{in}:{name}, or components/schemas/{name}/properties/{name} for a specification; {surface}/{tool}, then /inputSchema/properties/{name}, for the MCP catalog. A deprecated default appends /default to its parameter's schema pointer, a deprecated value /enum/<value>, and a deprecated value format (a class of values, such as timestamps) /format/<name>.

earliest_adaptation.description: The earliest date the adaptation this deprecation announces may ship. It is no earlier than 30 days after the release that publishes the deprecation; the gate holds the adaptation to whichever of the two is later. An ISO date, quoted in YAML so it stays a string.

value.description: For a deprecated value or default, the value that is deprecated.

follows_deprecation.description: The earlier deprecations this adaptation follows. Each names a release after 3.0 whose revision-history entry deprecates the element, at the pointer the adaptation withdraws or at an element containing it.

release.description: The MAJOR.MINOR release that published the deprecation.

surface.description: The published artifact the pointer addresses: the SAGE Core API specification, the CAS Application API specification, or the MCP tool catalog.

pointer.description: The element, in the contract comparison's pointer form: paths/{path}/{method}, then /parameters/{in}:{name}, or components/schemas/{name}/properties/{name} for a specification; {surface}/{tool}, then /inputSchema/properties/{name}, for the MCP catalog. A deprecated default appends /default to its parameter's schema pointer, a deprecated value /enum/<value>, and a deprecated value format (a class of values, such as timestamps) /format/<name>.

exemption.description: Why this adaptation ships without a deprecation, or before its window closes. It covers the change's withdrawing findings as a whole. The summary and for_callers also name it.

kind.description: security-exposure: serving the old form keeps a vulnerability, disclosure, or authentication weakness reachable. data-integrity: serving the old form lets callers write or read wrong data. never-served: the withdrawn element never reached a caller.

reason.description: The exposure, the integrity fault, or why the element was never served, stated so a reviewer can check it.
